cases.name: an-assertion-with-no-condition
cases.description: An assertion is the one construct whose whole worth is that it fails. Without a condition it never can, and the config carries a check that reads as verification and compares nothing.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert says="something"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-condition-that-is-only-whitespace
cases.description: Written but empty is the same as absent, and easier to produce by accident — a generated config, or an attribute whose value was edited away.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert that="   " says="something"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-assertion-with-nothing-to-tell-the-reader
cases.description: says= is what a person reads in a CI log months later. An expression on its own leaves them to reconstruct what property was being defended and why it mattered.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="Rows"><gen type="stat" of="N" op="count"/></sequence><assert that="Rows == 3"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-typo-in-a-column-name
cases.description: that= is the if= language, so a name that is not a name is the same mistake with the same code. An implementation that gave assertions their own name resolution would either invent a second code for one error or, worse, read the misspelling as literal text and check a string against a number.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="Rows"><gen type="stat" of="N" op="count"/></sequence><assert that="Rowss == 3" says="…"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-assertion-outside-env
cases.description: An assertion is a statement about the whole run, like <uniq> and <distinct>, so <env> is the only place it means anything. Inside a <sequence> it would be a claim about a column made from inside that column.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence></env><assert that="1 == 1" says="…"/><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-attribute-assert-does-not-read
cases.description: An assertion is its two attributes and nothing else, so a third is a typo for one of them rather than a setting. Ignoring it in silence would leave a config that looks like it says something it does not — which is the exact shape this whole tag exists to catch.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert that="_total == 3" says="…" wen="typo"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-assertion-with-both-that-and-each
cases.description: that= is read ONCE over whole-run values and each= is answered on every row. A tag carrying both leaves a reader to guess which of the two the sentence in says= describes, and the answer decides whether the run is checked once or a million times.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert that="_total == 3" each="N > 0" says="something"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-per-row-condition-that-is-only-whitespace
cases.description: The rule that catches an empty that= catches an empty each= too: written but blank is the same as absent, and easier to produce by accident.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert each="   " says="something"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-per-row-assertion-with-no-message
cases.description: says= is required of a per-row assertion for the reason it is required of a whole-run one: the sentence is what a reader is given in a CI log months later. Here it also names the row, and a row number with no sentence beside it says even less.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><assert each="N > 0"/></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-assertion-with-each-written-before-that
cases.description: The order the two are written in does not change the answer. An implementation that read whichever came first would accept this and refuse its mirror, which is a difference no rendering fixture could show.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="3" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence><sequence name="R"><gen type="stat" of="N" op="count"/></sequence><assert each="N > 0" that="R == 3" says="something"/></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>
